in_sanskrit.name: द्वारका
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Dwaraka is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Dwara' meaning 'gate' and 'Ka' meaning 'water'. It is also called 'Moksha Dwar' or the 'Gateway to Salvation'. The city is believed to have been founded by Lord Krishna himself.

in_hindi.name: द्वारका
in_hindi.long_meaning: द्वारका नाम संस्कृत के 'द्वार' से उत्पन्न है, जिसका अर्थ 'प्रवास द्वार' या 'धवाजा' है। यह भगवान कृष्ण ने अपनी ओछी से स्थापित किया गया था।

in_tamil.name: துவராகம்
in_tamil.long_meaning: The Tamil name for Dwaraka is 'Thuvaraagam'. The word 'Thuvara' in Tamil means 'door' and 'Agam' means 'abode'. So, Dwaraka in Tamil is interpreted as 'The Abode of the Door'.

in_telugu.name: ద్వారక
in_telugu.long_meaning: The Telugu name for Dwaraka is 'Dvaaraaka'. The word 'Dvaaraa' in Telugu means 'gate' and 'Aaka' means 'city'. So, Dwaraka in Telugu is interpreted as 'The City of the Gate'.

in_marathi.name: Dwaraka
in_marathi.meaning: हिंदू नाव म्हणजे City of Lord Krishna
in_marathi.long_meaning: Dwaraka हे एक हिंदू नाव आहे जे भारतीय संस्कृतीत खोल आध्यात्मिक महत्त्व ठेवते। The divine city where Lord Krishna resided, often described as a paradise on earth.

in_bengali.name: Dwaraka
in_bengali.meaning: হিন্দু নাম যার অর্থ City of Lord Krishna

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dwaraka" is synonymous with the legendary city built by King D Krishna, a shrine for Krishna devotees. This ancient city, believed to be situated on the western coast of India, holds immense cultural significance in Hindu mythology and literature. Dwaraka is depicted as the royal city, a center for learning, philosophical discussions, and spiritual growth, where Lord Krishna lived with his Yadav clan.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, Dwaraka is considered a realm of peace, righteousness, and happiness, where Lord Krishna manifested many of his divine Leelas or pastimes. It is said that by entering the realm of Dwaraka, one's mind attains purity, devotion, and fulfillment. Lord Krishna himself is considered as the embodiment of love, courage, and wisdom, and his presence in Dwaraka is symbolic of divine grace and protection. Thus, the name Dwaraka represents not only a physical place but also an emblem of peace, moral values, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Dwaraka is believed to be the capital city of the legendary king Krishna during the Mahabharata period. It is described as a magnificent city, built by the architect Vishwakarma and gifted to Krishna by Indra, the king of gods.

The archeological site of Dwaraka, located in the Gulf of Kutch, Gujarat, India, is believed to be the ancient city of the same name. It has yielded artifacts dating back to the Indus Valley Civilization, and is mentioned in various Jain and Hindu texts as an important center of trade and pilgrimage.

modern_usage.modern_context: Dwaraka, an ancient city mentioned in Hindu mythology and religious scriptures, continues to be a popular topic on various digital platforms. On Twitter, users frequently share stories, quotes and images related to the city and its significance in Hindu mythology. On Instagram, there is a growing community of travel bloggers sharing their experiences and photographs from the Dwaraka temples and other tourist attractions. On Google Maps, users can navigate through the Dwaraka city and explore its historical and religious sites, including the Dwarkadheesh Temple, Rukmani Temple, and Gomati Ghat.
